summary: harness continue reopens a lane from the newer of the box's and origin's branch (both merged if diverged); refuses a legacy run (code beyond its base) with three ways forward, exit 1, run.log + high-priority notification; under pr a dependent's PR waits (noted once), harness merge lands proposed milestones in order. 11 checks in 46-lanes-continue.sh.
verified_how: tests/checks/46-lanes-continue.sh 11/11 (6 of the first 8 red before the code; the 3 added after review red with their fix undone); full suite via check.sh: green in 383 s, 550 tests; bash -n on bin/harness lib/driver.sh lib/lane.sh lib/record.sh

dead_ends.tried: slot_open as P1-03 left it (local lane branch first)
dead_ends.why: a stale local branch after Michael pushed to origin made every lane push non-fast-forward; the stub's own push failed and the sessions read as usage limits

discoveries.text: Under MERGE_POLICY=pr a proposed milestone merged by Michael on GitHub was never seen as merged by the driver, so anything depending on it waited forever; merge_milestones now notes '<m> merged into main (by its PR)' when the tag is on main.
The legacy test is merge-tree of the run's base (origin/main or BASE_REF) and HEAD, diffed outside .harness/runs/, not the plan's merge-base diff; a --base run would otherwise be refused.

Once P1 merges, an automatic continuation of agent-harness-2026-10-26 run by the P1 driver is refused (this branch carries code main lacks): the refusal now reaches Michael as a high-priority notification.

questions: D13 default: the legacy refusal goes to stderr, run.log and a high-priority notification, not to harness-log.md (the CLI never writes the record). Want a harness-log note too?
D14 default: when the box's and origin's lane branch diverged, origin's is merged into the box's (a conflict is needs Michael). OK, or should origin's always win?
